triage_records.title: Treating chronic insomnia in postmenopausal women: a randomized clinical trial comparing cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia, sleep restriction therapy, and sleep hygiene education
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a randomized controlled trial that directly compares Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBTI) against Sleep Hygiene Education (SHE) in adults (postmenopausal women) with chronic insomnia. It reports outcomes at both post-treatment and 6-month follow-up, directly addressing the question of relative effectiveness and persistence of benefits.

triage_records.title: Insomnia Patients With Objective Short Sleep Duration Have a Blunted Response to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper investigates the efficacy of CBT-I in a specific subgroup (insomnia with short sleep duration) and reports follow-up data at 6 months. However, it does not directly compare CBT-I to sleep-hygiene education alone, which is the specific comparison requested in the research question. It provides indirect evidence regarding the persistence of benefits (follow-up data) and the differential response to the intervention, but lacks the head-to-head comparison with the control condition specified.

triage_records.title: Moderators of Cognitive Behavioral Treatment for Insomnia on Depression and Anxiety Outcomes
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a review of randomized controlled trials focusing on CBT-I for insomnia in patients with comorbid psychiatric disorders (MDD, GAD, PTSD). It does not directly compare CBT-I to sleep-hygiene education alone, nor does it primarily focus on the persistence of benefits at follow-up for the general insomnia population. Therefore, it does not directly answer the specific research question.

triage_records.title: Preventing postpartum insomnia: findings from a three-arm randomized-controlled trial of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, a responsive bassinet, and sleep hygiene
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a randomized controlled trial that directly compares Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) against a sleep hygiene control group. It reports on the effectiveness of CBT-I in reducing insomnia severity (ISI scores) and includes follow-up assessments at 2, 6, and 12 months postpartum, addressing both the comparative effectiveness and the persistence of benefits requested in the question.
